name: Piper / wyoming-piper TTS
description: Fast local neural text-to-speech (rhasspy/piper, now OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) built on VITS ONNX voices, most commonly exposed as a Wyoming-protocol server (wyoming-piper) for Home Assistant voice on TCP 10200. A binary/JSONL Wyoming protocol — NOT HTTP by default. An optional HTTP demo server (script/run_http) and third-party OpenAI-compatible HTTP wrappers also exist. No authentication in any variant.
auth_notes: No authentication in wyoming-piper, the Piper HTTP demo server, or common OpenAI-compat wrappers. The Wyoming protocol on TCP 10200 has no auth handshake at all — any client that speaks the JSONL protocol gets a full model description and can synthesize. Home Assistant add-on deployments assume the port is bound to a trusted LAN; hobbyist/self-host deployments frequently expose 10200 (or the 5000 HTTP demo) directly to the internet. Operators are expected to front it with a reverse proxy for any auth; most do not.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Wyoming protocol default port. High recall but low precision — 10200 is the whole Wyoming ecosystem (piper/whisper/openwakeword). Wyoming is a raw JSONL/binary TCP protocol, so HTTP http.html/http.title filters return 0 here; confirm the piper role via a Wyoming describe handshake at the banner/Censys layer, not the HTTP body.

The optional Piper HTTP demo server (script/run_http, port 5000) renders a simple synth form referencing Piper; HTML-body match. Low volume — most deployments run Wyoming, not the HTTP demo. FP risk: 5000 is a very busy port (Flask default, UPnP); the piper keyword narrows it.

Banner/raw-payload match on the Wyoming info response, which enumerates piper voice models. This is a Censys-route signal (Censys services.banner) more than a Shodan HTML signal; the string 'piper' plus a voice name in the TCP payload is the discriminator against whisper/openwakeword Wyoming servers on the same port.

Piper voice model naming convention (<lang>_<REGION>-<name>-<quality>, e.g. en_US-lessac-medium.onnx) appears in the Wyoming describe/info payload and uniquely identifies a Piper voice server versus other Wyoming roles. Censys-route (banner content), not Shodan HTML.

Version disclosure via the HTTP demo page or a wrapper /info route. Wyoming-piper version itself is only recoverable from the protocol describe payload (attribution.version field) — Censys-route for the TCP variant.

known_vulns: No authentication on the Wyoming TCP 10200 protocol — any client speaking JSONL can enumerate voices and synthesize unlimited audio at operator compute cost
No rate limiting — CPU/GPU compute-theft via automated synthesize floods; Piper is CPU-cheap but bulk abuse still exhausts host resources and enables mass audio generation
HTTP demo server (script/run_http, Werkzeug/Flask) is explicitly a demo — no auth, no input validation, not hardened for exposure
TTS-abuse: open synthesis endpoint is a free voice-generation backend for robocall/IVR spoofing, disinformation audio, and spam voicemail at scale
Model/voice enumeration leaks operator configuration (installed voices, languages) via the Wyoming describe response with no access control
Home Assistant add-on deployments that port-forward 10200 expose the voice pipeline of the whole smart-home to arbitrary synthesis injection
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) TTS-abuse — an open Piper/Wyoming endpoint is a free, unlogged, no-auth voice synthesis backend ideal for robocall scripts, vishing IVR prompts, and bulk disinformation audio; Piper's CPU-only speed makes high-volume abuse cheap for the attacker and costly (compute + reputation) for the operator. (2) Compute theft — no rate limiting means automated synthesize floods. (3) Configuration leak — the Wyoming describe response enumerates installed voices/languages with zero auth, aiding operator fingerprinting. (4) Smart-home pivot — Home Assistant deployments that forward 10200 expose the household voice pipeline. Lower data-sensitivity than STT/whisper (no inbound audio PII), but high abuse-as-a-service value. NOTE: the dominant deployment is a raw Wyoming TCP protocol, so Shodan HTTP-body dorks largely miss it — route population discovery through Censys banner content / active Wyoming describe probes.
deployment_notes: Dominant deployment is the Home Assistant 'Piper' add-on / rhasspy/wyoming-piper Docker image speaking the Wyoming protocol on TCP 10200 (binary + JSONL, NOT HTTP) — this is the exposure most 10200 hits represent. The OHF-Voice/wyoming-piper repo is the current upstream (rhasspy/wyoming-piper redirects there). An optional HTTP demo web server (script/setup --http then script/run_http) serves a Werkzeug/Flask form on port 5000 for browser testing — not intended for production. Third-party OpenAI-compatible HTTP shims (exposing /v1/audio/speech) and n8n integrations exist but are non-canonical. Voices are VITS ONNX files named <lang>_<REGION>-<name>-<quality> (e.g. en_US-lessac-medium). CPU-first: runs acceptably without a GPU, which is why it is the default HA TTS and why exposed instances are common on small VPS/SBC hosts.
